It's aimed at them, meaning it's made for them. Turn a book toward someone, now it's aimed at them, it's made for them. See the connection?" "The reading is the same as the word 向く so work off of that word to be able to read this one."

example_sentences.japanese: これは子ども向けの作ひんではないですよね。
example_sentences.english: This work isn’t intended for children.

example_sentences.japanese: このカレーは、日本人向けのあじですね。
example_sentences.english: This curry was made for Japanese tastes.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチが履いてるパンツは、子供向けなんじゃないのか？ツンツルテンだよ。
example_sentences.english: Aren’t the underpants Koichi is wearing for children? He’s outgrown his clothes.

english: Including, Included, Furnished With, Attached To
notes: "You know that the kanji 付 means attach and words like 付く mean ""to be attached."" This has the same idea. When you see this attached to another word, for example, you might know that something is attached to something else, or perhaps included with it. For example, if you stay at a hotel room, maybe it is a breakfast付き, i.e. ""including breakfast.""" "The reading comes from the reading of the kanji as well as from words like 付く and 付ける."

example_sentences.japanese: このそうじきは、一年間のほしょうしょ付きですよ。
example_sentences.english: This vacuum cleaner comes with one year warranty.

example_sentences.japanese: 一ぱく二食付きのりょかんをさがしています。
example_sentences.english: I'm looking for a Japanese style hotel that includes dinner and breakfast.

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋は冷蔵庫、洗濯機付きです。
example_sentences.english: This room is furnished with a refrigerator and a washing machine.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the on'yomi reading, which you learned. This is probably because you'll see this word attached to other words, showing the rank of that thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年は何位だろう？
example_sentences.english: I wonder where I'll rank this year.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは黒ニンニクのしょうひりょうにかんしては、ポートランドで一位かもしれない。
example_sentences.english: In terms of black garlic consumption, Koichi might be number one in Portland.

example_sentences.japanese: マラソン大会で一位になったので、両親がマウンテンバイクを買ってくれた。
example_sentences.english: I came in first at the marathon rally, so my parents bought me a mountain bike.

notes: "Throw this onto a number and you have yourself the number of times something has increased. For example, ３倍 means something increased ""three fold.""" "The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji. Omit the 〜 when writing out the answer, though. That just represents that there should be something before the kanji in this word when being used."

example_sentences.japanese: ワニカニのレビューの数が四倍になってしまった。
example_sentences.english: WaniKani's review count has quadrupled.

example_sentences.japanese: クリスマスの日ぐらい、きゅうりょうを十倍にしてくれたっていいじゃないか！
example_sentences.english: Why not just pay me ten times more than usual on Christmas day at least?

example_sentences.japanese: 回転寿司の普及に伴い、日本におけるサーモンの消費量は輸入開始から三倍となった。
example_sentences.english: Since the introduction and subsequent spread of conveyer belt sushi shops, salmon consumption in Japan has tripled.

english: As Much As You Want, All You Can
notes: "Just release the topic... let it go free! Let it do whatever it wants. Sometimes the topic will be food... if that's the case, just release yourself and do whatever you want with the food (eat it all!). If it's drinks, drink it all! This word has to do with doing whatever you want and as much as you want. You'll see this attached to ""all you can ____"" words, so look out for them in the next  couple levels." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べ放題に行くといつも食べすぎてしまいます。
example_sentences.english: Every time I go to an all-you-can-eat restaurant, I end up eating too much.

example_sentences.japanese: カラオケに行くなら、朝まで歌い放題のプランにしようよ。
example_sentences.english: If we go to karaoke, why don't we choose the plan where we can sing as much as we want until the morning?

example_sentences.japanese: もしテキストフグの永久購読権を購読されるのであれば、日本語の学習がし放題ですよ。
example_sentences.english: If you purchase a lifetime subscription to Textfugu you can study Japanese as much as you want.

english: Formal Name Ender, Formal Name Title, Sama, Very Formal Name Ender, Formal Name Suffix
notes: Add this onto the end of someone's name. It's probably too polite, to be honest, unless you're talking to one of your customers or something. It's good to know, but you're probably not going to use it, despite seeing and hearing it fairly often. The reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチ様は、何もかもが自分の思い通りにならないと気がすまないんですよ。
example_sentences.english: Koichi-sama can't stand it if everything isn't exactly the way he wants.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本で手紙を送る時には相手の名前に様をつけないと失礼になります。
example_sentences.english: It would be rude if you don't attach the formal name ender, sama, to the recipient's name when you send letters in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグのコウイチ様御一行九名様ですね。お席のご用意ができましたのでどうぞ。
example_sentences.english: Mr. Koichi from Tofugu, party of nine. Your table is ready.

notes: "Remember how 社長 is the company president? This uses the same 長 meaning (where it means something like ""boss""). Since 課 means section, this is the section manager." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 先月、課長にしょう進しました。
example_sentences.english: I got promoted to section manager last month.

example_sentences.japanese: 課長になれたのはうれしいんだけど、ざん業代が出ないから実はきゅう料が下がったんだよね。
example_sentences.english: I'm glad I was able to become a section chief, but my pay has actually decreased because I don't get paid for overtime.

example_sentences.japanese: 課長が少しうざいんだよね。他の社員に良い印象を与えようといつも頑張っちゃってさ。
example_sentences.english: My section manager is kind of annoying. He is always trying to impress the other workers.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. Usually this refers to a train station in particular, but can be any kind of station. "The kanji here uses えき as both its on'yomi and kun'yomi, so no worries here. You can go to this station or that station, and both stations will use the same reading as the kanji it comes from."

example_sentences.japanese: 新宿駅でおりて下さい。
example_sentences.english: Please get off the train at Shinjuku Station.

example_sentences.japanese: 上野駅の駅の前にはコウイチが一億円かけて出店したトーフグやきぎょうざの店があります。
example_sentences.english: There is a Tofugu pot sticker shop in front of Ueno Station that Koichi opened with one hundred million yen.

example_sentences.japanese: ようやく直接お話することができてよかったです。まさか駅でバッタリお会いするなんて思ってもいませんでしたよ。
example_sentences.english: It was nice finally talking to you in person. I never thought I would run into you at a station.

notes: "When you wrap around the entire  circumference of the year you've come back around to the start of it. This is the anniversary." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグは、来年で十周年になるので、コウイチは周年プロジェクトをけい画しています。
example_sentences.english: The next year is Tofugu's 10th anniversary, so Koichi is planning an anniversary project.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの実家は、にゅう牛の周年放ぼくをしています。今年は、放ぼく事業を始めてから、ちょうど二十周年です。
example_sentences.english: My family grazes dairy cow herds year round. This year is the 20th anniversary of their grazing business.

example_sentences.japanese: 今度の日曜日に、私達はマクドナルドでTofuguの五周年記念を祝います。
example_sentences.english: Next Sunday we’ll celebrate Tofugu’s fifth anniversary at McDonald’s.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it should use the kun'yomi reading. When learning the kanji, you didn't learn that reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you with this word: You are counting your bundles. There are a lot of them, so you have to create tabs (たば) in your notebook to properly categorize everything. Imagine yourself doing this (physically creating the tabs in your notebook, even though your notebook didn't come with tabs)."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは札束にうもれるほど金を持っている。
example_sentences.english: Koichi has so much money that he can swim in it.

example_sentences.japanese: 記おくが正しければ、たしかブロッコリーは束で売ってたと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: If I remember correctly, I think they sell broccoli in bunches.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてもコピー用紙がいるんだけど、この花束とそのコピー用紙一束を交換してもらえないかな？
example_sentences.english: I have to get some copy paper. Could you exchange a bundle of copy paper for this bouquet of flowers?

english: Circumference, Perimeter, Edge, Surroundings, Locality, Neighborhood
notes: "This is the noun version of the kanji circumference, so it means circumference too." "Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You really want to measure the circumference of something but there doesn't seem to be anything round around. That's when you remember, ""Mah Walnuts! (まわ)."" The walnuts in your pocket have an easy edge to measure."

example_sentences.japanese: 周りがギザギザになっているコインを集めています。
example_sentences.english: I'm collecting coins with serrated edges.

example_sentences.japanese: 大好きな事やむ中になれる事があるなら、周りが何と言おうと、それをやりつづけるべきだよ。
example_sentences.english: If there's something you love or are passionate about, you should stick with it regardless what the other people say.

example_sentences.japanese: 周りの目が気になるんです。
example_sentences.english: I'm worried about what other people are thinking about me.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: 性はんざいをゆるしてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: We must not forgive sex crimes.

example_sentences.japanese: 性による違いをはあくしたうえで、男女平どうを考えることが大事だと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think it's important to consider gender equality in order to understand actual gender differences.

example_sentences.english: Please mark whether you are a man, woman, or other under gender.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.english: The true commander of the Tofugu army is not Koichi, but Viet.

example_sentences.japanese: どうやっててき軍の追げきをかわせばいいんだ。
example_sentences.english: How could we evade the enemy troops' pursuit?

example_sentences.english: Let’s go back to the army base for now.

example_sentences.japanese: この遺跡には、竪穴住居郡があります。
example_sentences.english: These historic ruins contain a district of pit dwellings.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "The reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji. In fact, this kanji's on'yomi AND kun'yomi are しき, so you can never go wrong."

example_sentences.japanese: いったい式場はどこなんだ？
example_sentences.english: Where the heck is the ceremony being held?

example_sentences.japanese: 開会式は九時にスタートする予定です。
example_sentences.english: The opening ceremony is scheduled for 9 a.m.

example_sentences.english: The ritual was boring, so I killed time by solving a bunch of equations.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチは、大切にしていたダンボール箱がすてられたことを知って、顔面そう白になりました。
example_sentences.english: Koichi turned pale when he learned that his precious cardboard box had been thrown away.

example_sentences.japanese: 夫がトマトを箱で買ってきて、食べきれなくてこまっています。
example_sentences.english: My husband bought tomatoes by the crate and we're having trouble eating them all.

example_sentences.japanese: トーフグのオフィスに届いた箱の中には、辞書と死んだフグが詰まっていた。
example_sentences.english: The box that arrived at the Tofugu office was crammed with dictionaries and dead puffer fish.

notes: "The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The 〜 is there to show this attaches onto things, like 東京弁, meaning ""Tokyo Dialect.""" The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji. Because it's normally attached to other words it uses the on'yomi reading like a jukugo word normally would.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語で一番面白い方言は東北弁でしょうか？
example_sentences.english: Is Tohoku dialect the most interesting Japanese dialect?

example_sentences.japanese: 私は日本語の共通語も関西弁も話せるからバイリンガルなんですよ。
example_sentences.english: I am bilingual because I can speak standard Japanese as well as the Kansai dialect.

example_sentences.japanese: 博多弁で喋る女性はとても可愛いと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think women who speak with a Hakata accent are really cute.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. Lucky you, the word garden is read the same way as the kanji is read. Kind of a Garden of Eden for kanji and vocab, no?

example_sentences.japanese: 保育園を建てる前に、労働者たちが地面を固めました。
example_sentences.english: Laborers hardened the ground before building a daycare.

example_sentences.japanese: リンゴ農園でリンゴを箱づめするアルバイトをしていました。
example_sentences.english: I had a part-time job where I packed apples in boxes at an apple orchard.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は植物園の近くに住んでいます。
example_sentences.english: I live near the botanical garden.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "The reading is the same as the kanji. Now that is true kanji love."

example_sentences.japanese: サボテンの花は、母性愛のしょうちょうです。
example_sentences.english: The cactus flower is a symbol of maternal love.

example_sentences.japanese: 社内恋愛をもう想するのが好きなんですけど、一番最近の私のもう想の中ではコウイチとビエトの間に愛がめ生えちゃったんです！
example_sentences.english: I like fantasizing about office romance and in my latest fantasy, love grew between Koichi and Viet.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はお金は愛より大切だと思います。よく「愛があれば山でも動かせる」なんて言いますが、実際はお金が無いとそんなことできないでしょ。
example_sentences.english: "I think money is more important than love. They often say, ""love can move mountains,"" but in reality you can’t do that without money."

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: もう少しだけ、側にいてもいい？
example_sentences.english: Can I be with you a little longer?

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんの側をはなれちゃだめよ！
example_sentences.english: Don't drift away from mom, okay?

example_sentences.japanese: ソファの右側に植木を置こうかなと思ってるの。
example_sentences.english: I'm thinking about putting a potted plant on the right side of the sofa.

notes: "You'll see this attached to other words to make them plural. That's why it's called a pluralizing suffix. " "This is almost the same reading you learned with the kanji. Remember たつ? Well this is read たち. Here's a mnemonic to help you remember it:If you want to pluralize something, touch (たち) it to something else. One egg touches another egg, well now they're eggs. Plural eggs! One friend? No. Touch them! Touch them right on the face. Now there are two friends. Plural friends! Thanks to the good ol' pluralizing suffix touch!Oh, and don't type the 〜 out when writing the answer. It's just there to let you know that there's usually something attached to this word."

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチ達、一体どこに行ったんだろう。
example_sentences.english: I wonder where Koichi and the others went.

example_sentences.english: Those gangs are all Viet's sworn brethren.

example_sentences.japanese: あなた達はまだ未成年でしょう。
example_sentences.english: Aren’t you still minors?

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "The reading you learned with the kanji is the same as the reading for this word. No holes in your knowledge!"

example_sentences.japanese: はずかしくて、穴があったら入りたいよ！
example_sentences.english: I am so embarrassed, I wished I could sink into the floor!

example_sentences.japanese: あそこのほら穴には、コウモリが住んでいるらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that bats are living in the cave.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が深くて素晴らしい穴を掘れるのは、持って生まれた才能です。
example_sentences.english: He has the natural ability to dig deep, magnificent holes.

notes: "You have reason behind your theory, making it a real theory (unlike those that don't have reason, I guess?)." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチの理論はだれからも支持されませんでした。
example_sentences.english: Koichi's theory was not supported by anyone.

example_sentences.japanese: コウイチはよい会社の社長になるために、リーダーシップ理論を学んでいます。
example_sentences.english: Koichi is learning leadership theories in order to become a good company president.

example_sentences.japanese: 理論的に説明するのは苦手です。
example_sentences.english: I’m bad at giving theoretical explanations.

notes: "The main cause behind someone's righteousness is usually what isms or principles they believe in. Buddhism, Shintoism, socialism, communism, you name it. If you believe in one of those it's the main driving factor behind what you believe righteousness to be." This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: フグは肉を食べないよ。菜食主義者だからさ。
example_sentences.english: Fugu doesn’t eat meat. He’s a vegetarian.

notes: "Let us conserve our tasks. We will give it to the Ministry Of Tasks!" This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ビエト財務省国際局次長は現在ダイエット中であり、砂糖の代わりにサッカリンを用いているため、彼の食事には砂糖を使用しないでください。
example_sentences.english: Mr. Viet, Senior Deputy Director General, International Bureau, Ministry of Finance, is on a diet right now and substitutes sugar with saccharin, so don’t use sugar in his meal.

notes: "Even though the kanji mainly means  occasion, for some reason this word means side or edge. I suppose on occasion kanji takes you to the edge of what ought to make sense when it comes to kanji." "You're on the very edge of the world. You heard that at the edge of the world are the key words (きわ) written there in big fiery letters, telling you the meaning of life. Supposedly these are the words of God himself. They say: ""We apologize for the inconvenience."" WHAT? THESE ARE THE KEY WORDS???"

example_sentences.japanese: 小さい頃、友人達と毎日水際で遊んでいました。
example_sentences.english: When I was little, I would play by the water’s edge every day with my friends.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. Lucky for you, even though this word is a single kanji, it uses the same reading you learned, meaning you know how to read it already. Time to plan and scheme for your next vocab/kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 本日のプレゼンでは、主に3つの策を取り上げます。
example_sentences.english: In my presentation today, I will cover three main plans.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. "The reading is the same as the kanji, though it's kind of like an add-on for other words in a sense, which makes it behave like jukugo, I think. Don't confuse this with 各々 though. That one does use the kun'yomi reading, which is strange when you consider this one doesn't. Every kanji has its own ""perks"" I suppose."

example_sentences.japanese: まず始めに、各チームの代表者を決めて下さい。
example_sentences.english: First, choose a representative for each team.

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. The reading is the same as the reading you learned with the kanji... and you thought I was about to punish you because it was a single kanji vocab word. Now get over here. example_sentences.japanese: クラスの生徒全員がカンニングで罰を受けたなんて、信じられない。

notes: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

example_sentences.japanese: この絵に合う額を探しています。
example_sentences.english: I’m searching for a frame to match this picture.

example_sentences.japanese: ホッケーの競技場さえも、オゾン層の破壊に関係しているって、知ってたかい？

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は二歳の時に甘い咳止めシロップを一気飲みしてしまい、鼻から管を通して胃を洗浄するはめになった。
